overview: AI hardware and infrastructure face tighter scrutiny and supply constraints
AI-powered consumer devices add recording and transcription features
Regulatory and credit concerns rise around major AI firms

top.title: From spectrum to structure: Identifying molecules with Mass Spec Skills for Google Antigravity
top.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Mass Spec Skills, a tool that helps scientists interpret tandem mass spectra using Google Antigravity, aiming to speed molecular identification for research.

top.title: Nothing offers a full look at its AI earbuds and charging case
top.summary: Nothing unveiled Ear Note earbuds with a case that records, transcribes, and summarizes conversations, expanding AI note‑taking capabilities in consumer audio hardware.

top.title: OpenAI cuts GPT-6.2 usage: Astra hits limits 40% faster, Sol 25% faster
top.summary: OpenAI announced reduced usage limits for its GPT‑6.2 model, with Astra and Sol models reaching limits 40% and 25% faster respectively, tightening access to advanced models.

top.title: S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and ‘key man’ risks
top.summary: S&P Global is reviewing Nvidia’s credit rating over governance issues and reliance on CEO Jensen Huang, potentially lowering its rating and increasing borrowing costs.

top.title: AI data centers are becoming harder to build, and neoclouds are feeling it
top.summary: TechCrunch reports that building AI data centers is becoming harder as Nvidia demands near‑ready sites, causing delays and higher debt for emerging ‘neocloud’ providers.

top.title: Amazon is reportedly in talks to end Muse AI shopping block
top.summary: Amazon is in talks to lift its block on Meta’s Muse AI shopping agent, weighing potential impacts on ad revenue and product search quality before deciding.
